data.cultural_impact: The name Ashutosh is considered as a divine name in Hindu culture, bearers of this name are believed to have the fortune of their deepest desires being fulfilled. The name Ashutosh is revered and often given to children as a blessing for a prosperous and fulfilling future. Ashutosh is also linked with Hindu deity Lord Ganesha, who is known as the remover of obstacles, and is believed to fulfill the deepest desires of his devotees.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ashutosh holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism, it represents the deep inner yearning and longing for the fulfillment of one's desires and dreams. The name Ashutosh is a reminder that no matter how small or big our desires may be, they can and will be fulfilled with the grace of God and the power of our inner belief and devotion. It also symbolizes the idea of being content and satisfied with the present moment, while also maintaining the hope and faith for a better future. Ashutosh is not just a name, it is a powerful mantra that embodies the essence of faith, hope, and the promise of fulfillment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashutosh: Wish-fulfilling, ever hopeful. One who is constantly touched by divine grace and blessings.

vedic_reference.note: Ashutosh is a name of Lord Vishnu in Hinduism, which means 'The one who is not desirous of anything and is content with whatever he has'. It is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures like the Vedas, Puranas, and Upanishads.

historical_references.reference: Ashutosh was an epithet of the Hindu god Vishnu, meaning 'pleaser of the Gods' or 'whose heart is not touched by sorrow'. This name is mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, which is believed to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.

Ashutosh was also the name of a famous 19th century Indian philosopher and social reformer, Swami Vivekananda. He was a chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and is credited with introducing Hinduism to the Western world through his participation in the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893.
